method: Read all 245 complete frozen official Portuguese paragraphs and all 224 Portuguese notes. Compared the shared coverage policy and internal authoring instructions against local agency, scope, qualifications, attribution and theological premises. These records are not public reading copy or native-speaker proofreading. Exact contiguous Portuguese quotations have locally located UTF-16 coordinates, paragraph and span hashes. Counts and hashes establish integrity, not semantic fidelity; public prose requires its own complete comparison.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the generational choice between humane and dehumanizing construction; put creation and Incarnation behind an attributed foundations link so the secular entry does not imply that these premises are universally accepted.

Preserve collaboration and dialogue with all people and the attributed divine grounding. The frozen edition repeats diálogo diálogo; do not silently repair a quotation or turn the repetition into new content.

Locate the present letter in the living social-teaching tradition inaugurated by Rerum Novarum; remove the closing invocation while keeping the argument that proclamation cannot ignore concrete social life.
Carry forward technology's possible benefits, harms and uncertain long-term effects; separate the appeal to ask God for wisdom from the practical need to interpret current transformations.

necessaryQualifications.text: Technological benefits and harm are both possible; long-term effects are not fully predictable.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep regulation alongside the prior question of who controls technology; private transnational actors exceeding some governments' resources are part of the source's power analysis, not a reason to declare all private activity illegitimate.

necessaryQualifications.text: Adequate regulation is necessary but the question is not limited to regulation; ownership and power still matter.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve shared discernment of ends rather than a succession of emergency responses; the open questions ask a community to choose a direction, not predict an inevitable technological future.

Use Babel as an explicitly biblical interpretation of uniformity and self-assertion, preserving the distinction between coordinated activity and homogenization; do not present the narrative as empirical evidence about AI.

Retain Nehemiah's listening, distributed work and shared responsibility as the narrative's argumentative work; keep his historical prayer in optional biblical context rather than misclassifying the reported action as a prayer addressed to the reader.

Preserve both technology's useful possibilities and its dependence on the choices of designers, funders, regulators and users; relocate the Holy Spirit and biblical construction frame without claiming a morally neutral tool.
Retain the critique of profit that sacrifices the weak and of reducing people to data; explain the two biblical paths as attributed metaphors while preserving plurality as a resource for community.

Keep the explicit argument that common-good building rests on relationship with God in optional foundations; exclude Augustine's direct prayer without converting the theological desire for fullness into an identical secular claim.
Keep vulnerability and limits as features of human life rather than failures to erase; progress is evaluated by everyone's dignity and peoples' good, not simply by increased technical capacity.

Preserve cooperation across institutions and differences, including the claim that tensions can become creative under shared responsibility; collaboration is not an instruction to suppress disagreement.

necessaryQualifications.text: Shared responsibility must allow tensions and differences to become creative rather than suppress them.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Translate the demand for evangelical language into an attributed argument for truthful, non-humiliating communication; retain the institutional tasks of literacy, vulnerable-person protection and guiding research toward justice.
Use the appeal to remain human amid AI as orientation; keep Jubilee grace and humanity revealed in Christ as foundations rather than treating the ceremony as the source's main policy proposal.
Retain the call to plan, work and center people ordinarily excluded, while removing the direct prayer and implored blessing clauses; the common-good task must survive those exclusions.

Retain the historical development of social teaching as the author’s account: new situations challenge its categories, so IA demands development faithful to the Gospel rather than a mere appendix or emergency response.
Keep the Church's self-description as serving the common good and its distinct relationship to political communities; this explains the institutional speaker before presenting the sequence of popes.

Preserve the claim that religion cannot be relegated to private life and that the Church may comment on civil events; attribute that public-role claim rather than presenting it as an uncontested rule of politics.
Keep the acknowledgment of earthly realities' proper autonomy within the Church's theological account; do not erase either autonomy or the belief that the Spirit works within human endeavors.

necessaryQualifications.text: Earthly realities have proper autonomy even within the source's theological interpretation.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain the distinction between ecclesiastical and civil responsibilities and the warning that exceptional Church substitutions cannot become normal; this limits institutional scope rather than licensing permanent replacement of public institutions.

necessaryQualifications.text: Exceptional ecclesial provision cannot replace ordinary civil institutional responsibilities.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the twofold acknowledgment of earthly autonomy and different spheres of competence as the basis for engagement with sciences and cultures; preserve the Church's own stated purpose in that engagement.

Retain the welcome offered to sincere seekers of truth, goodness and beauty, with scientific inquiry and diverse expert opinions; do not replace openness to debate with a claim that the Church settles empirical disputes.

necessaryQualifications.text: Welcome diverse expert opinions; do not claim the source decides disputed scientific matters.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the distinction between orienting principles and technical solutions or competing economic/political models. The teaching offers help with shared judgement, not a replacement for political institutions.
Retain the request to confront past intolerance and violence in truth’s name. Truth as shared gift, time over occupied power and the polyhedron image do not imply unrestricted relativism.

necessaryQualifications.text: The source claims one Gospel truth viewed from different perspectives, not unrestricted relativism.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve cultural and historical plurality in the Church's account of catholicity; local contexts matter to application, even while the text maintains a universal vocation.

Keep the contrast between a handbook and a living process of discernment, including dialogue, memory and prophecy; do not paraphrase the continuing presence of the Incarnate Word as merely institutional learning.
Retain the transition to selected stages since Rerum Novarum as a guide to the timeline; do not promise a comprehensive history beyond the overview the author supplies.
Preserve the distinction between ancient Gospel reception and its modern systematization; the source does not describe social doctrine as spontaneously invented in the modern age.

Keep Rerum Novarum's worker dignity, association and wage concerns as the historical starting point; preserve its claim that evangelization has structural consequences rather than replacing it with a purely economic origin story.

Retain Quadragesimo anno’s structural critique, social purpose of property, fair wages, association, subsidiarity and opposition to totalitarianism; keep criticism of both unrestrained competition and collectivist suppression of responsibility.

necessaryQualifications.text: Preserve criticism of both unrestrained competition and collectivism that undermines individual responsibility.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep Pius XII's war-and-reconstruction context, law over force, intermediary organizations and international imbalances; this is an attributed historical account, not a claim that all those institutions worked as intended.
Preserve John XXIII's widening global focus and rights-based institutions and relations between peoples; do not reduce the development to a change of papal personnel.
Retain Vatican II's turning point, human dignity and pluralistic peaceful societies; the historical explanation must keep the concrete rights criteria rather than just celebratory Council language.
Keep Paul VI's account of peace as more than the absence of war, linked to humane development and poorer countries; do not treat economic growth alone as the definition of peace.
Preserve Octogesima Adveniens' engagement with postindustrial change and exclusion; the historical application requires that no person or people be treated as expendable.
Retain John Paul II's treatment of work amid ideological crisis, sufficient remuneration and participation; labor's personal dignity is more than its usefulness to production.

Keep North–South inequality, scrutiny of economic mechanisms and solidarity as political charity. The Portuguese source repeats the widening of the gap; convey the argument once in paraphrase and preserve the repetition only in exact quotations.

Retain Centesimus Annus' reflection after the Soviet collapse together with continuing exploitation and representation crises; do not turn the passage into unconditional endorsement of whatever markets or democracies do.

necessaryQualifications.text: The historical market/democracy discussion remains qualified by exploitation, exclusion and representation failures.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep Benedict XVI's widening of development and the political community's irreplaceable responsibility; this limits a reading in which growth alone or private generosity supplies the common good.
Preserve charity joined to truth and its critical public role; the text does not define charity as private sentiment detached from institutions or justice.
Keep Francis' account of history through hopes and vulnerabilities and the Church's learning from the poor; the poor are participants in the institution's transformation, not merely recipients.

Retain integral ecology joining environmental harm and the cry of the poor, work, intergenerational justice and dialogue of politics and economics. The local sentence repeats o clamor da terra and o clamor dos pobres with a missing connecting verb; paraphrase the clear relationship without fabricating a repaired quotation.
Keep Fratelli Tutti's response to fragmentation, conflict and pandemic in the account of fraternity; its broad social friendship must not be narrowed to the author's own religious group.
Retain the conclusion that social teaching responds to concrete history while preserving an internal core; the overview invites attention to coherence, not a claim that no historical tensions exist.
Introduce the principles as interrelated within a living teaching in dialogue with history, cultures and sciences; individual concept cards must not imply that each principle stands alone.

necessaryQualifications.text: Principles must be considered together; isolated cards cannot make them independent rules.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain the call to lay people and all people of good will to embody the principles in daily life, families, work and civic action, and the distinct encouragement to higher education, theological/philosophical research and the teaching office.
Keep the Trinity as the stated source of received and shared love in optional foundations; it is a theological premise, not another name for interpersonal cooperation.
Preserve the Incarnation and Spirit-led life as the Christian grounding of social consequences; moving this explanation to foundations must not imply that the ethical claims had no religious basis.
Keep being created in God's image as the source's account of personhood and the person as the Church's way; retain that rationale separately from the secular statement of unconditional worth.

Preserve the transition from uniqueness and dignity to rights inherent in being human; the authority cited is John Paul II and the Church's teaching, not an unqualified legal claim about every jurisdiction.

necessaryQualifications.text: Rights are grounded in being human rather than granted as a reward for performance.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Define moral, social, existential and ontological dignity separately; the first three can vary while intrinsic worth cannot be diminished, with creation and divine love retained as the optional grounding.

necessaryQualifications.text: Moral, social and existential dignity can change; ontological dignity belongs to every person and cannot be lost through sin, failure, humiliation or exclusion.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the claim that fundamental dignity is not earned or extinguished, even by moral failure; attribute its foundation and resist turning other kinds of diminished dignity into diminished human worth.

necessaryQualifications.text: No search for a person's failings can erase intrinsic worth; attribution retains the declaration's religious grounding.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve gratitude for the historical identification of rights and the duty of international protection; rights are concrete expressions of intrinsic dignity, not merely a list of admired aspirations.

Keep universal rights and the source's explicit life-from-conception-to-natural-end position, including abortion and euthanasia, through clear Church attribution; secular navigation must not erase contested normative commitments.

necessaryQualifications.text: Attribute the life-from-conception-to-natural-end, abortion and euthanasia positions to the Church without silently broadening or hiding their scope.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep both dangers: rights declared only formally despite actual violations, and failure to sustain their universal foundation through inquiry; fearfully manipulated apparent consensus cannot establish legitimate protection.

necessaryQualifications.text: Name both formal rights without practical protection and the lost foundation of universality; manipulated apparent consensus does not resolve either danger.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep minority rights and women's equal dignity together with the continuing exclusions named by the author; a general equality slogan would lose the test of concrete treatment.
Preserve the priority of each person and family over grand ideological declarations; decent work, protections and necessities are the practical test of proclaimed dignity.
Keep the move from inalienable personal dignity to obligations toward society; contributing within one's ability protects participation without demanding identical capacity from everyone.

necessaryQualifications.text: Contribution is within the limits of each person's ability; unequal ability does not diminish dignity.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Use the Council's definition of social conditions enabling fulfillment for groups and individuals; retain the common good's moral dimension rather than presenting it as aggregate convenience.

necessaryQualifications.text: The common good concerns conditions enabling fulfillment for groups and individuals, not merely summed preferences.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the whole's surplus over a sum of interests as an argument about shared life; do not turn the metaphor of a plus into a calculable metric or disregard individual persons.
Retain a people as a living reality formed through a shared vision and agreements; participation and differences remain part of that vision rather than enforced unanimity.

Keep the State's responsibility for cohesion, unity and fair organization of civil society, harmonizing interests without leaving the weakest behind. The Portuguese critique names short-term calculations and estéreis polarizações, followed by lost credibility, inequalities and social fractures.
Keep the international extension of the common good and rejection of eliminating or subjugating a nation; widening divisions are part of the source's diagnosis, not permission for domination.
Retain the universal destination of both material and cultural goods; explain its creation-based grounding in foundations while preserving access and benefit beyond any one owner.

Keep the recognized right to private property and its subordination to the universal destination of goods; neither absolute ownership nor a claim that all property is denied is faithful to this doctrinal position.

necessaryQualifications.text: Private property has a recognized right, meaning and purpose, but is not absolute and remains subordinate to the universal destination of goods.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Extend universal goods to patents, algorithms, platforms, infrastructure and data. Preserve environmental regulation, the poor and future generations, and the local warning evitando desperdícios e novas formas de pilhagem (waste and plunder), without importing Spanish estafa wording.
Keep the paired duties not to supplant local actors and positively to protect, promote and coordinate them; subsidiarity is both a limit on takeover and a requirement of support.

necessaryQualifications.text: Do not supplant lower-level actors; positively protect, promote and coordinate their freedom and creativity.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve necessary State intervention and civil-society responsibility together; the paragraph explicitly rejects interpreting subsidiarity as State disengagement.

necessaryQualifications.text: Subsidiarity explicitly does not justify State disengagement; necessary intervention enables civil actors without permanently replacing them.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep decisions as close as possible to affected people and their meaningful involvement before choices are fixed; preserve support for intermediary associations rather than substituting individual consultation alone.

necessaryQualifications.text: Decisions should be taken at the closest possible level to affected people; support and participation are conditions, not mere delegation.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Apply subsidiarity to platform and corporate power, not only governments; independent checks, algorithm transparency, data access and recourse are concrete safeguards for meaningful participation.

necessaryQualifications.text: Power at the highest level can be corporate/platform power; participation includes independent checks, algorithm transparency, equitable data access and recourse.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain State and transnational safeguards that let varied communities help govern data and algorithms; local agency depends on wider cooperation rather than a handful of actors setting all rules.

necessaryQualifications.text: State and transnational safeguards enable community agency; cooperation must respect differing levels and joint responsibility.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep solidarity as recognition of interdependence turned into real responsibility and shared decisions; it requires more than an expression of sympathy.
Distinguish factual digital interconnection from deliberately chosen cooperation and mutual care; being connected does not by itself satisfy the virtue of solidarity.

necessaryQualifications.text: De facto digital interdependence must become consciously chosen cooperation and care.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve solidarity as both institutional principle and personal virtue, including choices about consumption and technology that impede others' dignity; do not confine it to charitable feeling.

necessaryQualifications.text: Solidarity is both an objective social principle and a personal virtue, with consumption responsibilities.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep global obligations and future generations within the assessment of technological decisions; benefits for an immediate minority cannot exhaust the evaluation.

necessaryQualifications.text: Global and intergenerational impacts matter beyond the benefit for an immediate few.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain just conditions for everyone, especially the weakest, while placing following Jesus and Gospel fidelity in foundations; justice remains a structural demand rather than private benevolence.
Explain the preferential option for the poor through the groups the source names; preserve the priority of those most excluded without recasting it as a hierarchy of intrinsic human value.
Keep structural injustice, prevention and support for people still bearing past harms; correction after damage cannot replace fair structures or historical responsibility.

necessaryQualifications.text: Prevention of structural injustice and concrete support for past victims complement individual moral responsibility.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Apply social justice to networks, platforms and technological power; the passage asks that dignity and common good shape the digital environment rather than profit alone.

Keep migrants and refugees as the test of social justice, including safe legal routes and integration together with the right to remain safely at home; preserve displaced people's agency, resources and dreams rather than treating migration as one homogeneous problem.

necessaryQualifications.text: Protect safe legal routes and integration for those displaced, and the right to remain safely at home by addressing root causes; people retain agency and resources.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain all people and the whole person, all dimensions of existence and future generations. The local paragraph has one [110], with no English comparison-HTML extra marker.
Retain development as both right and duty with minimum enabling conditions, diverse peoples and ways of life; development is not imposed cultural uniformity.

necessaryQualifications.text: Minimum enabling conditions and respect for peoples' diverse ways of life belong to development as both duty and right.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep ecological responsibility, disadvantaged communities and those who follow us as inseparable conditions; technological gain cannot excuse degraded living conditions or environmental harm.

necessaryQualifications.text: Ecological responsibility and future generations limit what can count as integral development.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Use integral development as the evaluative frame for digital innovation, including IA; the paragraph connects the preceding principles to later judgements instead of adding a separate technological ethic.

Preserve the Church's demand to apply its own principles internally, especially transparent decisions, accountable responsibilities and evaluation; keep the synodal mission as attributed institutional context rather than removing self-examination.

necessaryQualifications.text: The Church must apply transparency, accountability and evaluation within its own structures, not only demand them of others.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain real participation of the baptized and intermediary Church bodies, not nominal committees; name the ecclesial audience and the rejection of paternalism so this is not falsely generalized as an already achieved practice.

necessaryQualifications.text: Ecclesial participatory bodies must be genuine rather than merely nominal; do not claim that the desired condition already exists.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep sacramental communion as the Church's stated source of solidarity and diversity within unity; this is theological explanation without a direct prayer, not material to discard under the devotional rule.

necessaryQualifications.text: Sacramental unity is the stated Christian foundation; diverse sensibilities are a richness on condition they remain anchored in unity as both gift and responsibility.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve all named forms of abuse, listening to victims, acknowledgment, reparation, prevention, shared resources and corrective assessment; the Church's religious mission must not screen its concrete duties from the secular main path.

necessaryQualifications.text: Retain spiritual, economic, institutional, sexual, power-based and conscience abuse; listening, harm acknowledgment, just reparation, prevention and corrective evaluation are distinct tasks.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain the transition to technology already present in daily life. The Portuguese source explicitly says this concerns the present, not a choice about the future; do not reverse that temporal emphasis.

Preserve discernment as continuing rather than settled once for all, with people called to build humane relations together; keep Gospel motivation distinct from the practical need for renewed judgment.
Explain the technocratic paradigm as the reduction of nature and people to objects serving efficiency; retain its attribution to Francis and distinguish that critique from blanket rejection of tools.
Keep increased technical power alongside the failure to learn to use power well; the listed fields describe a convergence of capabilities, not evidence that each field inherently harms people.

Retain the warning that achievements can turn against humanity and that performance can become the chief measure of people; the source evaluates the direction of progress rather than opposing progress categorically.
Keep concentrated control over platforms and infrastructure as shaping dependence and exclusion; do not reduce structural power to an individual user's choice of good or bad use.
Retain the social principles as criteria for judging concentrated digital power; the ensuing account of AI must remain connected to that framework rather than stand as a technical encyclopedia.
Preserve the author's explicit limit on scope: this is neither a comprehensive AI treatment nor a literature survey; human conscience and freedom guide the discussion of uses and limits.

necessaryQualifications.text: The author expressly provides neither a comprehensive treatment of AI nor a review of its literature.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep rapid technical change and the dual need for scientific research and moral discernment; timestamp source claims rather than silently updating them or claiming technical finality.

necessaryQualifications.text: Claims about rapidly changing AI must remain source-dated; scientific research and moral/spiritual discernment have distinct roles.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the author's distinctions between statistical adaptation, human experience and moral conscience, while labeling the categorical claims about AI's inner life as the source's position rather than settled scientific consensus.

necessaryQualifications.text: The categorical denials of experience, embodiment, conscience and understanding are the author's claims, not a scientific-consensus label; computation can nevertheless be effective and beneficial.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve both AI's value as a tool and vigilance about substituting simulated attention for relationships; the concern includes a possible loss of desire for human connection, not a claim that every interaction causes it.

necessaryQualifications.text: Risks include losing the desire for human connections; possible harm is not universal inevitability.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep AI's cross-sector usefulness together with environmental costs and the call for lower-impact solutions; benefits must not erase material dependencies.

necessaryQualifications.text: Potential benefits coexist with environmental impacts and a duty to reduce them.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain effects on rights, opportunities and status and the danger of models reproducing designers' stereotypes; this frames deployment as a social judgment, not purely a technical optimization problem.

Preserve the critique of unaccountable algorithmic judgments about who is worthy and the disappearing political choices behind them; classification never removes the need for accountable human decisions.
Keep moral choices embedded in data, models and objectives before use; evaluating what a system was designed to do is necessary alongside evaluating a user's behavior.

Keep clear responsibilities through design, training, use and delegation. Opacity complicates attribution and correction; the local responsabilização (accountability) explicitly requires identifying who must prestar contas, give reasons, undergo oversight and contestation, and repair damage.

necessaryQualifications.text: Responsibility extends across design, training, authorization, use, explanation, monitoring, challenge and remedy.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep prudence and sometimes slower adoption as responsible progress, supported by legal frameworks and independent oversight; generic ethical appeals are insufficient against infrastructure power.

necessaryQualifications.text: Prudence and sometimes slower adoption serve progress; legal frameworks and oversight are needed alongside ethics.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain public deliberation about the ethical code and shared social justice criteria as an additional requirement beyond machine alignment. Communities must still be able to participate and question values imposed by a few.

necessaryQualifications.text: Machine alignment does not replace public deliberation about ends, participation or the right to question decisions.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep unequal resources, community participation in decisions and oversight, and explicit regulation of data ownership. The author calls for creative common or collective management because many people contribute data; do not reduce this to distributing hardware.
Apply the principles to data and computational power with justice built into design; later repair remains important but cannot substitute for fair initial structures.

necessaryQualifications.text: Justice must shape design from the outset; post-deployment repair alone is insufficient.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Explain disarming AI as freeing it from an adversarial mentality and making it accessible and welcoming; retain the author's argument that regulation alone is insufficient, without mistaking the metaphor for a technical weapon-removal procedure.

Keep the developer's responsibility to consult affected communities and discern genuine good; put participation in divine creation in foundations rather than using it to bless innovation automatically.

necessaryQualifications.text: Possible participation in divine creation does not morally validate every innovation; affected communities and genuine good remain tests.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain the question of safeguarding humanity when people see themselves as optimization projects; relationship and communion limit performance-based pictures of the person.
Keep the warning against absolutizing any single human dimension, including intelligence; the claimed disorder can arise from disproportionate excess as well as scarcity.
Preserve civilization's test of care and the person as a subject of relationships and decisions; technical assistance can serve care without replacing responsible human presence.

necessaryQualifications.text: Care includes human subjects' own decisions; assistance must not erase relationship or agency.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Introduce the cultural narratives of enhancement and human-machine hybridity before their evaluation; label this as the author's framing of a debate rather than an exhaustive taxonomy.

Keep the plurality of transhumanist and posthumanist currents, the qualification about more radical forms and their often speculative status; do not attribute a single extreme program to everyone using either term.

necessaryQualifications.text: Both terms cover diverse currents; especially radical posthumanism and often speculative ideas must not be generalized to every adherent.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve the distinction between human-centered use of technology and a vision that devalues limits or ranks lives by usefulness; criticism targets the guiding outlook rather than all technological assistance.

necessaryQualifications.text: The object of criticism is the underlying vision; integrating technology in human-centered relationships is explicitly different from devaluing human limits.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain the explicit duty to try to eliminate suffering alongside acknowledgement of constitutive finitude. Attribute the faith-based interpretation and avoid implying treatment refusal or imposed avoidable suffering.

necessaryQualifications.text: The French source says it is our duty to try to eliminate suffering while acknowledging constitutive finitude; neither side authorizes refusing treatment or imposing avoidable suffering.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep compassion and the possibility of wisdom and closeness amid loss and failure; divine presence and worship are the source's additional religious interpretation, not a guarantee that suffering improves everyone.

necessaryQualifications.text: The source describes possible growth and closeness amid vulnerability, not a promise that every loss produces wisdom.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve the author's strong philosophical claim about suffering, love and desire as an attributed argument; connect it to the neighboring permission to relieve suffering rather than presenting it as clinical advice.

necessaryQualifications.text: Attribute the philosophical claim about suffering and love, and keep §118's approval of relieving suffering visible; this is not clinical advice.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep moral evil, possible conversion and Frankl's contrast between perpetrators and victims; the historical reference to prayer is not a prayer to remove, and hope must not excuse atrocity.

necessaryQualifications.text: Reported prayers of historical victims are narrative testimony, not a devotional formula to perform or censor; conversion must not excuse atrocities.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve vulnerability as a possible opening to fraternity and art's resistance to normalized evil; keep the named works as interpretive examples, not evidence that all audiences react alike.

necessaryQualifications.text: The named artworks are interpretive examples resisting normalized evil, not proof of uniform audience effects; accepting vulnerability is not glorifying harm.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain institutions protecting common life, contested moral progress and its reversibility. The frozen Nações Unidas(1945) lacks a space; preserve it in quotations without treating typography as an extra claim.

necessaryQualifications.text: Institutions protecting rights are fragile achievements sustained by responsible people, not evidence of inevitable historical improvement.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep particular movements and witnesses of human dignity as examples of change; the selected figures illustrate the source's claim and are not a complete or uniform account of world history.

necessaryQualifications.text: The named movements and figures are selected examples from different contexts, not an exhaustive history or a claim that every outcome had one cause.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve hidden service and perseverance alongside public witnesses, with religious communities and named believers as actual examples; do not turn credible witness into a purely technological mechanism of progress.

necessaryQualifications.text: Hidden service, perseverance and credible witnesses are part of the source's account; do not assign miraculous inevitability to particular outcomes.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the welcome for progress that relieves suffering on condition it preserves relationship and love; distinguish this practical condition from the Christian answer locating fulfillment in grace.

necessaryQualifications.text: Welcome technological relief and new possibilities provided relationship and love are preserved; divine grace is a distinct foundation.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the account of self-transcendence through divine gift and the Spirit, including Aquinas' disparity between created nature and divine life; secular self-improvement is not an equivalent paraphrase of grace.

necessaryQualifications.text: Grace surpasses created capabilities and is received as divine gift; do not paraphrase it as technologically achievable self-upgrading.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep grace and communion as theological premises while retaining the contrast between algorithmic correction and a person's possible transformation through error; the person's future is not to be treated as exhausted by a prediction.

necessaryQualifications.text: Algorithmic correction and personal transformation through error are contrasted; grace and relational freedom cannot be translated as statistical optimization.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Preserve Christian humanism's welcome for science under common-good and care criteria, with both conditional outcomes of technological progress; neither automatic optimism nor blanket fear represents the text.

necessaryQualifications.text: Christian humanism welcomes science; progress is accepted conditionally by its human effects, with both favorable and dehumanizing possibilities retained.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Use Augustine's two loves as an attributed moral interpretation of personal and institutional priorities; preserve the inward challenge without confusing two cities with a geographic or partisan division.

necessaryQualifications.text: The two cities are Augustine's moral/theological metaphor, not named territories or parties.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep the three announced application areas together: truth in public life, work's dignity and freedom from dependence and commercialization; the chapter is broader than employment alone.

Keep both rational verification against sources and relational trust as conditions for factual truth. The Portuguese edition repeats the requirement of averiguação, correspondência com as fontes e responsabilidade argumentativa; paraphrase once without silently repairing source quotations.
Keep resource-rich actors' influence over opinion and the need to pursue truth; the source diagnoses concentrated communicative power rather than claiming that all mediated opinion is fabricated.
Retain truth's enabling role in democracy and the warning about losing distinctions between fact and fiction; do not convert this into a demand that everyone share a political opinion.
Keep communication as cultural formation rather than information transfer alone; the online world affects lived relationships and imagination, especially among young people.
Preserve platform power over collective imagination and the positive goal of inner freedom and critical thought; a communication environment can nurture rather than dominate readers.

Keep the distinct duties of public rules, social/cultural institutions, schools/families and universities: transparency, privacy, journalism, verification, critical use and integration of knowledge. Truth as common good does not mean ownership by powerful actors.

Preserve journalists' role in exposing Church abuse and the institution's duty to confront uncomfortable facts without external compulsion; do not sanitize the source's shame or transfer responsibility to reporters.

necessaryQualifications.text: Journalists exposed Church abuse, but vigilance and transparency remain primarily the Church's own responsibility; victims' voices and institutional shame remain explicit.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep education's importance amid manipulation and the fatigue that discourages seeking truth; distinguish the diagnosed pressures from an assertion that young people are inherently incapable of thought.
Preserve patient engagement with reality and the warning that convenient AI answers can make thinking seem unnecessary; do not state that every use of AI blocks learning.

necessaryQualifications.text: AI convenience can make thought seem superfluous; it does not follow that every educational use has that effect.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain the source's concerns about early unsupervised exposure, bullying and sensitive images with source date and attribution; its appeal to literature is not a substitute for current clinical guidance or a universal diagnosis.

necessaryQualifications.text: The source's literature-based diagnosis concerns early and unsupervised exposure; timestamp and attribute it instead of presenting universal clinical advice.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep parents' limited ability to resist attention markets and the need for shared safeguards and literacy; assigning the whole duty to families would change the passage's institutional agency.

necessaryQualifications.text: Parents alone cannot withstand attention-market pressures; institutions and shared safeguards carry duties too.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain parents’ primary and inalienable right to choose education in accordance with their moral, cultural and religious convictions, alongside expectations of schools for relationships, critical thought, values and questions of meaning. Attribute this normative claim and do not score belief.

necessaryQualifications.text: Preserve parents’ primary and inalienable educational choice in accordance with moral, cultural and religious convictions, attributed to the source. Understanding is not assent.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Retain inequalities in educational access and the duty to make schooling accessible regardless of family resources; the socio-political challenge must remain visible beside pedagogical concerns.
Keep the pedagogical challenge of integral formation and critical, creative use of technology; catching up with devices is not the same as educating a person.
Preserve intellectual discipline, reading and careful analysis as conditions for inner freedom; do not promise an effortless atlas that replaces the intellectual work the text values.
Keep the shared educational alliance among families, schools, Christian communities and public institutions; retain time and trustworthy relationships as things technology alone cannot supply.

necessaryQualifications.text: Shared time and trustworthy relationships cannot be supplied by technology alone.

coverage.reviewInstruction: Keep work's protected dignity and its capacity for shared achievement; Benedict's union of prayer and work is historical religious context, not a liturgical formula to delete.
Preserve work's personal value and the allowance for emergency financial assistance; the limitation concerns aid as the sole response, not condemnation of every form of income support.

necessaryQualifications.text: Emergency financial assistance can be necessary; it is criticized only as the sole response. Work's dignity is not a condition for a person's intrinsic worth.

reviewContext.text: A Magnífica Humanidade criada por Deus encontra-se hoje perante uma escolha decisiva: erguer uma nova torre de Babel ou construir a cidade onde Deus e a humanidade habitam juntos. Cada geração recebe em herança a tarefa de dar forma ao seu tempo: de fazer amadurecer a história como um lugar onde a dignidade de cada pessoa seja salvaguardada, a justiça promovida e a fraternidade possibilitada. Sobre cada época, porém, paira o risco de construir um mundo desumano e mais injusto. Onde a humanidade corre o perigo de perder a sua identidade, nós, cristãos, erguemos os olhos para o Deus feito carne, sabendo que «o mistério do homem só no mistério do Verbo encarnado se esclarece verdadeiramente». reviewContext.text: Alicerçados em Cristo, a pedra viva, experimentamos a poderosa e misteriosa ação do Espírito Santo e acreditamos que todo o autêntico esforço humano de cooperar com Ele para o bem será abençoado pelo Pai celeste, no qual depositamos a nossa esperança. Por isso, com determinação, podemos contribuir em todas as iniciativas que constroem um mundo mais justo e convidar outros a colaborar conosco na promoção do desenvolvimento integral de cada ser humano. Desejamos entrar em diálogo com todos os homens e mulheres do nosso tempo, com os quais partilhamos os acontecimentos, as questões e as aspirações da humanidade. Essa abertura ao diálogo diálogo é parte integrante da vocação da Igreja, pois ela, constituída em Cristo «como que o sacramento […] da íntima união com Deus e da unidade de todo o género humano», [3] reconhece na história o lugar onde o Evangelho interpela e acompanha a experiência humana.
